newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moldovan 1996 grains harvest far below 1995 level.
newsitem.headline: Moldovan 1996 grains harvest far below 1995 level.

text.p: Moldova's drought-hit grains harvest, excluding maize, was 850,000 tonnes this year, half of 1995 level and the amount officials had predicted, a senior Agriculture Ministry official said on Thursday.

"Our data show that the country harvested a mere 850,000 tonnes of grain crops except for maize, compared to 1.7 million tonnes last year," Ion Popovici, in charge of the ministry's crops growing department, told Reuters.
Popovici said Moldova's overall grains harvest, including maize, could drop this year to 1.6-1.7 million tonnes from 2.38 million in 1995 after maize is gathered later this month.
"This year's harvest figures may be adjusted later, as we continue to receive complete harvest reports from northern districts, but I do not expect any big changes," Popovici said.
Ministry figures put the 1996 wheat harvest at around 750,000 tonnes.
"Maize was sown this year on some 200,000 hectares, and initially we counted on yields of 3.5-4.0 tonnes per hectare, but non-stop rains in Moldova's north could reduce yields," Popovici said.

An official from the state Cereale grain-purchasing company, who declined to be identified, said he thought the government would ban grain exports until state reserves were filled with 240,000 tonnes of wheat.
"As for grain exports, there has been no official document signed so far (calling for a ban)," he said.
But he said the state had stopped issuing export licences.
The government has so far purchased 170,000 tonnes of wheat from farmers at 1,000-1,200 lei per tonne.

"But in fact, grain producers are paid only half the price -- another half is written off for their debts to the budget, for fuel and for spare parts for their harvesting equipment," the Cereale official said.
He declined to say if Moldova would resort to any grain imports in the coming months.
But Deputy Prime Minister Valeriu Bulgari has said the country could import 100,000 tonnes of wheat form Kazakhstan.
Moldova has not said whether it will re-tender for 35,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat under the PL-480 programme after it cancelled buying late last month.
